entries.title: Searching for the interpretation that changes the interpretation
entries.summary: A direct statement of purpose and a method for comparing canonical and noncanonical evidence without collapsing manuscript dates, canon history and empire.

entries.title: How the argument developed: Jesus, resurrection and empire
entries.summary: Trace the historical-Jesus hypothesis, Paul, later Gospel narratives, countertexts and the move to a first-century imperial question.

entries.title: Early creeds, angels and resurrection evidence
entries.summary: Examine 1 Corinthians 15, Philippians 2, Colossians 1, Hebrews 13 and angelic hospitality, separating early testimony from later interpretive claims.

entries.title: Imperial pressure and the Gospel Pilate
entries.summary: Compare Gospel portrayals of Pilate with Philo and Josephus, testing accommodation and anti-imperial readings without assuming state authorship.

entries.title: Jesus, Resurrection Theology and Imperial Capture: the conversation
entries.summary: The November 6 dialogue, including every prompt, both pasted-text attachments, and the replies on Mark 9, John 12, Mark 12 and imperial pressure within the Gospel narratives. Original wording and historical qualifications are preserved.

entries.title: Would Jesus Oppose the Resurrection Gospel?
entries.summary: A historical and theological thought experiment about Easter, authority, and whether resurrection proclamation can displace Jesus’s teaching on kingdom, mercy, and transformed conduct.

entries.title: Early resurrection accounts and source criticism
entries.summary: Compare Paul, Mark, Matthew, Luke and John, distinguishing the development of textual claims from independent verification of what happened.

entries.title: Christianity After Bodily Resurrection?
entries.summary: Explore faith, community and Christian formation when bodily resurrection is reinterpreted, with attention to a wider religious inheritance.

entries.title: Prophecy, recurring patterns and the corrective word
entries.summary: A working chapter on Daniel, Newton and the Four Horsemen as resources for a recurring-pattern model, centered on truth and repair.

entries.title: Prophecy, partial success and causal feedback
entries.summary: A working chapter separating partial predictive success, belief-mediated fulfillment, historical meaning and claims of divine revelation.

entries.title: Testing recurring prophetic patterns
entries.summary: A proposed mathematical research protocol, a limited register audit, and reproducible synthetic examples. The examples are synthetic, not empirical validation of the framework.

entries.title: Iran infrastructure cascade inquiry
entries.summary: An inquiry into an Iran infrastructure cascade scenario, preserved alongside the event forecast register.

entries.title: Trump and Prophetic Signs: A Documented Timeline
entries.summary: A documented timeline for examining claims about Trump and prophetic signs.

entries.title: Public executions, religious justification and John 16:2
entries.summary: A study of public executions and religious justification in relation to John 16:2.

entries.title: Earlier-Teacher and Displaced-Biography Hypothesis
entries.summary: An overview of the Earlier-Teacher and Displaced-Biography hypothesis.

entries.title: From Exodus to Temple: competing chronologies
entries.summary: Substantive update examining the Joseph-before-Hyksos chronology.
